blocks.text: At Kunsthalle Münster in Germany, Mozambican artist Euridice Zaituna Kala explores colonial memory, historical erasure and the voices that persist beyond official narratives.

What happens to the histories that archives fail to preserve? In ‘Daylighting: aber es ist Wasser, das spricht’, Mozambican artist Euridice Zaituna Kala examines the relationship between memory, colonialism and the enduring consequences of historical erasure.

Presented at Kunsthalle Münster, the exhibition marks Kala’s first institutional solo presentation in Germany, bringing together installations, performances, paintings, objects and books that challenge established historical narratives.

Drawing on personal memories and archival research, Kala investigates how histories are constructed, whose experiences are documented and which voices remain unheard. Her practice engages with the representation of Black bodies in colonial archives, questioning the power systems that determine visibility and remembrance.
Bringing together ecological, feminist and Indigenous perspectives, the exhibition considers the connections between historical injustice, collective memory and contemporary struggles.

Previously presented in Rennes and Brussels, the exhibition has evolved through its engagement with each location. For Münster, Kala introduces new works that extend her investigation into the relationship between place, history and belonging.

Curated by Merle Radtke, ‘Daylighting’ invites audiences to reconsider the archive not as a fixed record of the past, but as a contested space where forgotten histories can be recovered and re-examined.
This exhibition is on view at Kunsthalle Münster , in Germany, until 24 January 2027.
